# Subnational official-stream research

Latest follow-up: [652-body evidence register](2026-10-23-comprehensive-followup.json). Current local catalogue 198 sources / 100 regional jurisdictions;45 scoped institutional URL gaps remain. Earlier snapshots below are superseded where counts differ. Full live/room/rights/accessibility certification is not complete.

Latest follow-up: [Corrientes and institutional metadata](2026-10-23-metadata-followup.md).
57 further institutional URL gaps resolved; 118 remain. Corrientes has two separate
chamber viewing links; Chubut’s directory-listed host remains an unexpected-content
hold. Current JSON records retain exact scope, evidence and follow-up actions.

23 October follow-up: [all 652 eligible bodies now have metadata/stream screening
and explicit gaps](2026-10-23-eligible-metadata-stream-audit.md). Twenty-two
institutional URLs were filled; 175 remain. The JSON ledger holds the current
per-body evidence; earlier search observations below remain dated history.

Research date: 2026-10-22. Jurisdictions searched: **1122 / 1122 currently inventoried**. The global inventory is **still expanding**.

Current authority register (23 October): **652 eligible; 458 outside scope;
ten specific legal evidence holds; two historical predecessors**. All 392
former generic cases received a disposition; ten legal questions remain open.
[Decisions and exact evidence needed](2026-10-23-authority-completion.md) ·
[Eligible-service queue and exclusions](2026-10-23-legislative-priority.md).
The 1,122 records include the new Korean successor and its two predecessors;
these are discovery records, not current-legislature or usable-stream totals.

Broad discovery across the 71 maintained Tier 1/Tier 2 country audit groups, including regional bodies and special-status territories. The public catalogue is restricted by legislative authority; discovery rows are not counts of eligible parliaments.

Establish jurisdiction inventory from official directories, then run a jurisdiction-specific official-source video and committee search. Record source-page access separately from active-media, event/room identity and rights validation. Never treat a pending inventory row as researched.

A search result is a lead, not a verified live stream. A successful page fetch is not a playback, room-identity, rights or schedule validation. Country scope dispositions distinguish no core regional legislature established from unresolved inventories. Discovery counts are not eligible-parliament counts; apply docs/catalogue-scope.md.

Country groupings for related territories are research associations, not sovereignty assertions. Read each constitutional relationship and scope note. The remaining-country source-check files record primary-source access attempts; they do not certify complete country inventories.

An inventoried body is not automatically a primary law-making parliament. First-level regional deliberative councils are labelled separately; ordinary municipalities are outside this pass unless they also perform the first-level role. Special-status and related territories require explicit relationships.

## Assembleia Legislativa da Região Autónoma dos Açores — Portugal

Status: **searched**. Inventory source: https://www.calrenet.eu/members/.

Catalogue eligibility: **eligible_legislature**. Constitution Articles 227 and 232 give the autonomous regions substantive regional legislation and reserve its exercise, regional budget, accounts and specified fiscal powers to their Legislative Assemblies. This covers the Azores and Madeira, not ordinary Portuguese municipal assemblies.

Catalogue eligibility: **eligible_legislature**. The Constitution and current Ministry of Territorial Policy explain autonomous-community self-government through their statutes and legislative assemblies. The ministry’s comparative statutory parliament chapter covers all17 communities’ legislation, budget and government control. They qualify as autonomous legislatures; Ceuta and Melilla have distinct statutes and are not included in this decision.

## Glarus — Switzerland

Status: **searched**. Inventory source: https://www.bayern.landtag.de/parlament/kooperationen/parlamente-in-der-schweiz/.

Catalogue eligibility: **eligible_legislature**. Current official cantonal constitutional text Articles82/89 identifies the Landrat as parliament and supreme supervisory body: it prepares Landsgemeinde legislation, enacts authorized ordinances, and can legislate urgently pending the next Landsgemeinde. Article90 gives budget/accounts powers. The Landsgemeinde itself enacts constitutional/statutory law. This is a cantonal legislative system, not a municipal assembly.

## Drenthe — Netherlands

Status: **searched**. Inventory source: https://organisaties.overheid.nl/14557/Provincie_Drenthe.

Body class: `regional_legislative_assembly`. Relationship: `first_level`.

Catalogue eligibility: **eligible_legislature**. The councils have autonomous provincial ordinance-making powers, initiative and amendment rights, budget authority and executive accountability/inquiry powers. Binding rules can apply directly to residents and businesses. National-law limits and the term verordening do not negate legislative authority. Municipal councils also have ordinance powers but remain outside the geographic scope.

Published official viewing links: `netherlands-drenthe-provincial-council`. Official provincial parliament meeting archive, with plenary and Statencommissie agendas and public recordings. The 30 September 2026 plenary page offers dated video excerpts; a public excerpt decoded at 1920x1080 with advancing playback. Current on-air live coverage was not tested.

Body class: `regional_legislative_assembly`. Relationship: `first_level`.

Catalogue eligibility: **eligible_legislature**. The current Local Government Act Articles 2, 25–28 and 35–36 establishes first-level councils’ autonomous ordinances, including rules affecting residents’ rights/obligations and administrative penalties, budgets and executive questioning. The Presidency explicitly identifies six special municipalities, thirteen counties and three cities as the first self-governing tier and their councils as legislative branches. These 22 qualify under the regional-ordinance rule; township councils and obsolete provincial consultative bodies do not follow by analogy.

Institutional website: https://www.mtcc.gov.tw/

These 22 qualify under the regional-ordinance rule; township councils and obsolete provincial consultative bodies do not follow by analogy. ## Seoul — South Korea

Status: **searched**. Inventory source: https://mois.go.kr/eng/sub/a03/citiesProvinces/screen.do.

Body class: `regional_legislative_assembly`. Relationship: `first_level`.

Catalogue eligibility: **eligible_legislature**. Local Autonomy Act Articles 28, 32, 47 and 49 establish first-level City/Do councils’ ordinances, budget/accounts, executive inspection and veto/reconsideration machinery. They qualify under the regional-ordinance rule; rights/obligations/penalties require statutory authority. Special self-governing provinces retain their separate enabling Acts. Ordinary Si/Gun/Gu municipal councils are not included.

## Jihočeský kraj — Czech Republic

Status: **searched**. Inventory source: https://crr.gov.cz/media/odkazy/.

Body class: `regional_deliberative_council`. Relationship: `first_level`.

Catalogue eligibility: **eligible_legislature**. Constitution Article 104 distinguishes higher territorial self-government and gives its assemblies generally binding ordinances. The Regions Act 129/2000 separates independent regional legislation from delegated state administration and reserves ordinances and budget to the elected assembly. These regional assemblies meet the substantive regional-ordinance rule. Prague qualifies in its combined regional capacity under Act 131/2000, not every municipal council.

## Banskobystrický kraj — Slovakia

Status: **searched**. Inventory source: https://mirri.gov.sk/mpsr/irop-programove-obdobie-2014-2020/kontakty-irop/kontakty-so/.

Body class: `regional_deliberative_council`. Relationship: `first_level`.

Catalogue eligibility: **eligible_legislature**. Constitution Articles 68–69 and Act 302/2001 sections 8–11 distinguish generally binding regulations in a self-governing region’s own affairs from regulations needing express delegation for state administration. The elected assembly approves regional regulations and budget and elects the chief controller. The eight higher-territorial assemblies qualify under the autonomous regional-ordinance rule, subject to national law.

## Dolnośląskie — Poland

Status: **searched**. Inventory source: https://polskieregiony.pl/konwent-przewodniczacych-sejmikow-wojewodztw-rp/.

Body class: `regional_deliberative_council`. Relationship: `first_level`.

Catalogue eligibility: **eligible_legislature**. Constitution Article 94 and the Voivodeship Self-Government Act Articles 18 and 89 vest elected sejmiki with generally binding regional local-law enactments, budget and executive-control decisions. This qualifies under the regional-ordinance rule, with the explicit statutory limits on lawmaking; it is not sovereign state legislation. A wojewoda’s executive regulations are a different institution.

## Abra — Philippines

Status: **searched**. Inventory source: https://psa.gov.ph/classification/psgc/provinces?vcode=82.

Body class: `provincial_legislature`. Relationship: `first_level`.

Catalogue eligibility: **eligible_legislature**. RA7160 section468 expressly identifies the Sangguniang Panlalawigan as the provincial legislative body with ordinances, appropriations, revenue/regulatory powers and provincial-ordinance penalties. This is a first-level province, not a municipal/barangay council. National-law limits do not negate the substantive regional authority under the same rule used for Japanese and Dutch ordinances. Website identity, current public proceedings and permissions remain separate.

Scope note: Separate provincial council proceedings from the governor's press events. Highly urbanized/independent-city councils and Metro Manila's coordinating council require their own scope review.

- [Primary legislative-authority framework](https://ldr.senate.gov.ph/sites/default/files/2022-12/RA%207160.pdf) — official_statutory_or_institutional_review. RA7160 sections16,22,468; Bangsamoro provinces are separately retained under BAA49 rather than mechanically applying this conclusion.

Catalogue eligibility: **eligible_legislature**. Constitution Article 18(3), (5) and (6) establishes elected regional representative councils and autonomous regional regulations. Aceh qanun/DPRA, Yogyakarta privileges, Jakarta’s transitional name/status and the Papuan DPRP/DPRK/MRP distinctions require exact institution and event identification before any viewing-service addition. ## Berat — Albania

Status: **searched**. Inventory source: https://www.instat.gov.al/en/documentation/classifications/version/level/?levId=3840.

Body class: `regional_council`. Relationship: `first_level`.

Catalogue eligibility: **outside_default_scope**. Constitution Article 110 identifies qark as the regional coordination/harmonisation tier composed from municipalities. Act 139/2015 assigns development-policy coordination and norms/standards for its allocated functions. These twelve indirectly composed county councils are administrative coordination bodies, despite generally binding decisions, budgets and public meetings; they do not establish substantive autonomous regional legislation.

Catalogue eligibility: **outside_default_scope**. Constitution Articles 71–78 describe regional democratic councils as local democratic organs for area management/development. The Local Democratic Organs framework and published delegation order concern local-authority administration and district by-laws. Binding local decisions, elected membership and development budgets do not establish autonomous general regional legislative powers. Exclude ten RDCs under the local/administrative-government rule.

Binding local decisions, elected membership and development budgets do not establish autonomous general regional legislative powers. Exclude ten RDCs under the local/administrative-government rule. Status: **searched**. Inventory source: https://verkiezingen.gov.sr/storage/pdf/Grondwet.pdf.

Body class: `district_representative_council`. Relationship: `first_level`.

Catalogue eligibility: **eligible_legislature**. Constitution Articles 169–173 entrust district household regulation to district councils. Regional Organs Act Articles 12–13 assigns district ordinances and executive information/scrutiny; its financial chapter adds district budgets. These ten first-level councils pass the regional-ordinance gate; village/resort councils do not follow by analogy.

Body class: `district_representative_council`. Relationship: `first_level`.

Catalogue eligibility: **eligible_legislature**. Constitution Articles 169–173 entrust district household regulation to district councils. Regional Organs Act Articles 12–13 assigns district ordinances and executive information/scrutiny; its financial chapter adds district budgets. These ten first-level councils pass the regional-ordinance gate; village/resort councils do not follow by analogy.

Scope note: Constitutional district representative council. District commissioners' administrative service areas are not one-to-one with district councils; exclude lower ressort councils.

Searches:
- Districtsraad (vergadering OR live OR video OR commissie)
- Commewijne Suriname Districtsraad (vergadering OR live OR video OR commissie)

Sources:
- [Inventory membership reference (not a broadcast check)](https://verkiezingen.gov.sr/storage/pdf/Grondwet.pdf) — inventory_evidence_only. This reference establishes the inventory lead only. The recorded jurisdiction-specific searches did not yield an accepted institutional broadcast page; no source access or absence of broadcasts is claimed.
- [Authority completion: surinamese-constitutional-district-ordinance-councils](https://www.dna.sr/media/18316/grondwet_suriname.pdf) — legislative_scope_framework. Constitution Articles 169–173 entrust district household regulation to district councils. Regional Organs Act Articles 12–13 assigns district ordinances and executive information/scrutiny; its financial chapter adds district budgets. These ten first-level councils pass the regional-ordinance gate; village/resort councils do not follow by analogy. The readable Regional Organs Act reproduction is consolidated to 2002, checked with the government’s 2025 constitutional publication. This confirms the legislative class, not every currently implemented financial mechanism or an actual sitting. Body class: `district_council`. Relationship: `first_level`.

The Local Government Act and the government’s National Decentralisation Policy classify district councils within local government, responsible for devolved services, district planning and coordination. These are not additional provincial or autonomous lawmaking parliaments. Apply the local/service-government exclusion to all ten districts.

Scope note: District council representation, distinct from district administration, community councils and Maseru's city council. Resolve current institutional pages before treating a video as council proceedings.

The Local Government Act and the government’s National Decentralisation Policy classify district councils within local government, responsible for devolved services, district planning and coordination. These are not additional provincial or autonomous lawmaking parliaments. Apply the local/service-government exclusion to all ten districts. ## Antioquia — Colombia

Status: **searched**. Inventory source: https://microdatos.dane.gov.co/index.php/catalog/643/variable/F12/V606?name=U_DPTO.

Body class: `departmental_assembly`. Relationship: `first_level`.

Catalogue eligibility: **eligible_legislature**. Constitution Articles 299–300 and Departmental Regime Act 2200/2022 Article 19 give departmental assemblies general ordinances, subsidiary police norm-making outside reserved national law, taxation/budget and executive scrutiny. These substantive binding regional norms meet the regional-ordinance rule despite their constitutional politico-administrative designation. The 32 departmental assemblies qualify; capital municipal councils do not qualify by analogy.

Scope note: DANE supplies the 32 department and capital names; Law 2200/2022 supplies the departmental assembly role. Distinguish assembly from governor and city council. The San Andrés archipelago is one department.

The recorded jurisdiction-specific searches did not yield an accepted institutional broadcast page; no source access or absence of broadcasts is claimed.
- [Authority completion: colombian-departmental-ordinance-assemblies](https://www.cancilleria.gov.co/normograma/compilacion/docs/constitucion_politica_1991.htm) — legislative_scope_framework. Constitution Articles 299–300 and Departmental Regime Act 2200/2022 Article 19 give departmental assemblies general ordinances, subsidiary police norm-making outside reserved national law, taxation/budget and executive scrutiny. These substantive binding regional norms meet the regional-ordinance rule despite their constitutional politico-administrative designation. The 32 departmental assemblies qualify; capital municipal councils do not qualify by analogy. This does not equate departmental ordinances with sovereign national statutes or certify any stream. San Andrés retains its special ethnic/territorial framework; only its departmental assembly is covered here.
- [Authority completion: colombian-departmental-ordinance-assemblies](https://www.funcionpublica.gov.co/eva/gestornormativo/norma.php?i=177869) — legislative_scope_framework. The 32 departmental assemblies qualify; capital municipal councils do not qualify by analogy. This does not equate departmental ordinances with sovereign national statutes or certify any stream. San Andrés retains its special ethnic/territorial framework; only its departmental assembly is covered here.

## Bogotá, D.C. — Colombia

## Bangkok — Thailand

Catalogue eligibility: **outside_default_scope**. Primary government materials classify provincial administrative organisations and Bangkok as local government, distinct from central/provincial state administration. These local administrative councils are excluded under the catalogue’s ordinary-local-government rule; local ordinances and budgets alone are insufficient. This is a scope classification, not a claim they have no normative or elected powers.

## Lop Buri — Thailand

Status: **searched**. Inventory source: https://www.nso.go.th/public/e-book/Statistical-Yearbook/SYB-2025/54/.

Body class: `provincial_administrative_council`. Relationship: `first_level`.

Catalogue eligibility: **outside_default_scope**. Primary government materials classify provincial administrative organisations and Bangkok as local government, distinct from central/provincial state administration. These local administrative councils are excluded under the catalogue’s ordinary-local-government rule; local ordinances and budgets alone are insufficient. This is a scope classification, not a claim they have no normative or elected powers.

Scope note: Elected PAO council, distinct from appointed governor and municipal/subdistrict councils. Bangkok has a separate metropolitan council; Pattaya is a special-city exception, not an extra province.

Catalogue eligibility: **outside_default_scope**. Primary government materials classify provincial administrative organisations and Bangkok as local government, distinct from central/provincial state administration. These local administrative councils are excluded under the catalogue’s ordinary-local-government rule; local ordinances and budgets alone are insufficient. This is a scope classification, not a claim they have no normative or elected powers.

Scope note: Elected PAO council, distinct from appointed governor and municipal/subdistrict councils. Bangkok has a separate metropolitan council; Pattaya is a special-city exception, not an extra province.

## Yasothon — Thailand

Status: **searched**. Inventory source: https://www.nso.go.th/public/e-book/Statistical-Yearbook/SYB-2025/54/.

Body class: `provincial_administrative_council`. Relationship: `first_level`.

Catalogue eligibility: **outside_default_scope**. Primary government materials classify provincial administrative organisations and Bangkok as local government, distinct from central/provincial state administration. These local administrative councils are excluded under the catalogue’s ordinary-local-government rule; local ordinances and budgets alone are insufficient. This is a scope classification, not a claim they have no normative or elected powers.

Scope note: Elected PAO council, distinct from appointed governor and municipal/subdistrict councils. Bangkok has a separate metropolitan council; Pattaya is a special-city exception, not an extra province.

## Western — Sri Lanka

Status: **searched**. Inventory source: https://www.parliament.lk/en/home/parliament-news/view/5121.

Body class: `provincial_council`. Relationship: `first_level`.

Catalogue eligibility: **eligible_legislature**. Constitution Article 154 G empowers each provincial council to make provincial statutes on the Ninth Schedule Provincial Council List; Article 154 F establishes a Board of Ministers responsible to that council. These nine are constitutionally devolved legislatures, separate from municipal, urban and Pradeshiya Sabha local councils.

Scope note: Retain institutional inventory despite dissolved terms/election delays. Parliament's March 2026 report discusses a legal obstacle to elections. Verify current sitting status individually; governor/administration videos do not establish an elected council broadcast.

## Emberá-Wounaan comarca — Panama

Status: **searched**. Inventory source: https://revistas.udelas.ac.pa/index.php/karakol/pueblos.

Body class: `indigenous_traditional_congress_or_council`. Relationship: `indigenous_governance_in_panama`.

Catalogue eligibility: **eligible_legislature**. The enacted Organic Charter (Executive Decree 84/1999) Articles 13–15 establishes the General Congress and gives it territorial regulations, sustainable resource-use regulation, budget approval, chief/board election and removal, and accountability/sanctions. This customary territorial norm-making and control passes the legislature criterion. The consultative Nokora council and ordinary municipal bodies are distinct.

Scope note: One of twelve congress/council structures listed by MINSA and public university UDELAS; not twelve equal first-level administrative units. Includes comarca, collective-land and people-wide institutions; legal level requires individual confirmation.

Organic Charter Decree 414/2008 Articles 9, 12, 26–27 and 89 establishes binding comarca-wide decisions and residual customary rule-making, executive reporting/removal and financial misconduct controls; Article 82 provides Congress revenues.
